transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08 16:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Ivy Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (CISO, Helix), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Maya Singh (Identity Eng), Derek Holt (Legal), Rajiv Menon (Infra - joined late)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Walked through SAML/SCIM steps, provisioning policies, RBAC matrices, audit/tracing and encryption options. Several action items captured.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ivy Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick us off. Quick agenda — run through the SSO runbook we emailed, SCIM provisioning behavior, then Marco will share an RBAC pattern and we'll hit audit/logging and KMS stuff.
[00:18] Sofia Patel: Sounds good. We're tight on time so, um, quick note: our goal is to have a pilot with a single team on 12/15 and then roll out broader next quarter. SOC 2 is in flight so we need evidence of audit trails and least privilege.
[00:35] Marco Alvarez: Great, worth noting Redwood supports SAML 2.0 IdP initiated and SP-initiated, and SCIM 2.0 for user/group sync and deprovision. The runbook we sent includes the endpoint URIs and a sample assertion.
[00:52] Liam O'Connor: Quick question — can SCIM handle group-to-role mappings? We prefer group-based role assignment so we don't have to maintain bindings in two places.
[01:05] Marco Alvarez: Yes, you can push groups via SCIM with the group->role mapping on our side. There's an optional mapping layer; by default we map SCIM group.displayName to a role namespace, but we can accept a mapping file during pilot.
[01:18] Maya Singh: How are you handling deprovisioning? We need immediate revocation when someone leaves.
[01:26] Marco Alvarez: Deprovisioning is supported with immediate account disable on SCIM delete and we also have token TTLs; for long-lived sessions we recommend session revocation hooks. Note, sometimes the transcript or docs say "KV cash" — that's our internal kv cache/kv-cache for fast prefix cache — sorry for the audio glitch.
[01:48] Sofia Patel: Also can you speak to the RBAC model? We want least privilege by default — dev/test/prod separation and a service account model for CI.
[01:58] Marco Alvarez: Absolutely. We generally recommend three axis: functional roles (viewer, editor, admin), environment scoping (dev/stage/prod), and service accounts with scoped capabilities. I'll sketch a sample matrix for Helix.
[02:12] Ivy Chen: I'll share an example matrix after the call, Marco will include binding examples for Helm/K8s service accounts and API keys.
[02:20] Derek Holt: On the legal side, we need to confirm data residency options and whether logs that include PII can be excluded from customer-facing artifacts. Also encryption at rest details — do you offer customer-managed keys?
[02:36] Marco Alvarez: For hosted we offer Redwood-managed keys, and for Private Dedicated or on-prem we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS/HSM integration. We can provide an encryption whitepaper.
[02:48] Liam O'Connor: If we go hosted, can we restrict logs to region-specific storage? Our compliance requires EU residency for EU customers.
[02:58] Ivy Chen: Yes, regional tenancy is available for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have EU regions — we can ensure data storage in the EU region and provide log export config. We'll capture that in the runbook.
[03:12] Maya Singh: Audit logs — what granularity, and how long can we retain? We need immutable logs for 12 months as part of SOC 2.
[03:23] Marco Alvarez: We emit audit events for auth events, model calls with metadata (request ID, user token hash, model ID — PII is redacted), config changes, and role changes. Retention for hosted defaults to 90 days, but enterprise packages can extend to 365 days and we can stream logs to your SIEM (Splunk/CloudWatch/Datadog) for longer retention.
[03:45] Sofia Patel: Are there redact options? Some logs contain email addresses in the user principal sometimes.
[03:52] Marco Alvarez: We redact cleartext PII by default in higher tiers; you can also route raw logs to your own S3 bucket with your lifecycle rules.
[04:03] [noise] Rajiv Menon: (joining) Sorry, just joined — quick q: does the RBAC role map support inheritance or just flat roles?
[04:10] Marco Alvarez: We support role hierarchies (inheritance) and policy-based scoping. For complex policies we can integrate with OPA via a sidecar for evaluating fine-grained policies, but that's more of a Private deployment pattern.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: On SAML metadata — we need the SP metadata file and assertion requirements (nameid format, audience). Can you send that?
[04:36] Ivy Chen: Yes — action item: we'll send SP metadata and the runbook with assertion examples and required attributes (email, displayName, groups).
[04:44] Derek Holt: Encryption — is there FIPS or HSM support for keys in your Private offering?
[04:51] Marco Alvarez: HSM-backed KMS is supported on Private and Dedicated with FIPS-mode options for key storage. We can provide attestation docs.
[05:02] Sofia Patel: On procurement timing — legal will need SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 docs. Can you point us to the artifacts and typical timeline for SOC evidence?
[05:12] Ivy Chen: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary, plus an evidence package for the maturity checks. Typically we share the latest available report and then provide a gap remediation plan if applicable.
[05:22] Maya Singh: Regarding SCIM scoping — can we limit which attributes are synced? For privacy we only want necessary attributes.
[05:30] Marco Alvarez: Yes, attribute filters are configurable. We support allow-listing and attribute transformations in the provisioning pipeline. We'll include examples in the runbook.
[05:42] Liam O'Connor: Do you support Just-In-Time provisioning instead of SCIM?
[05:47] Marco Alvarez: We do support JIT for SAML as an alternative — it'll create users on first login and you can combine with group claims for role assignment, but deprovisioning is best with SCIM.
[05:58] Sofia Patel: Auditability question — how do you surface evidence for auditors? Do you produce exportable logs and config snapshots?
[06:06] Marco Alvarez: We provide downloadable audit exports (JSON/CSV) for a time range and a configuration change history with diffs. For enterprise customers we can agree export cadence.
[06:17] Derek Holt: On contract language: need assurance on data deletion timelines post-termination and SLA for log delivery. I'll send a list of specific clauses.
[06:26] Ivy Chen: Noted — Derek, include that in the legal action item.
[06:30] [08:10] Ivy Chen: Ok, Marco do you want to walk through a quick example mapping?
[08:15] Marco Alvarez: Sure. Example: SCIM group "helix-devs" -> role "app.editor" scoped to workspace "helix-dev". Service accounts get roles via explicit binding; we recommend short-lived keys for CI with automatic rotation.
[08:32] Maya Singh: For CI keys, can you force rotation via API?
[08:36] Marco Alvarez: Yep, we expose a keys API and rotation endpoints, plus you can tie rotation to AWS Secrets Manager or Vault.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: Are audit events for key rotation captured?
[08:48] Marco Alvarez: Yes — key create/rotate/revoke are logged as audit events with actor and request ID.
[08:55] Sofia Patel: Anything else on residency? We have EU and APAC customers, want to limit cross-border movement.
[09:03] Ivy Chen: For Dedicated we can pin physical capacity to regions. For hosted, we can ensure customer data is provisioned in the requested region and provide contractual data transfer caveats.
[09:14] Rajiv Menon: Small nit: latency for EU region — do you offer edge routing or regional peering?
[09:21] Marco Alvarez: We have regional endpoints and peering options; for low-latency we'd recommend a dedicated pool in the region.
[09:28] Derek Holt: Anything around encryption in transit? We need TLS 1.3 and mutual TLS for some endpoints.
[09:34] Marco Alvarez: TLS 1.3 is supported, and mutual TLS can be enabled for private endpoints in Dedicated/Private deployments.
[09:42] Ivy Chen: Ok, recap — next steps: Ivy to share SP metadata & runbook, Marco to produce RBAC matrix, Helix to provide IdP group list and legal questions. We'll aim for a pilot auth smoke test 12/15.
[09:57] Sofia Patel: That works. Also please share the SOC and ISO docs.
[10:02] Ivy Chen: We'll attach those to the follow-up email and upload to your shared drive.
[10:06] [crosstalk] Marco Alvarez: I'll include examples for SCIM filters and a sample mapping file.
[10:12] Sofia Patel: Great, thanks everyone.
[10:16] Ivy Chen: Thanks all — we'll send notes and the artifacts.
[10:20] Derek Holt: Thanks, bye.

End transcript.
